dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?

Hi, Denise. Yes, my name is Ileana Rivera, and I'm calling about the water that sits on my street. I want to tell you from the beginning, because it's been going on a while. So last Monday, a week ago today, it was dry, no rain, nothing, and I came out to go to work and there's this pond across the street in front of the drain.
Okay. And no storm, no rain around that time?

None. That's the thing. Nothing fell from the sky. It had been cold and dry for days. Then Tuesday it was still there, Wednesday still there. Hold on, sorry, I'm typing myself a note and I know this phone picks up the keys like I'm shouting. Can you hear that clicking?
I can, it's pretty loud. That's okay, go ahead, or stop typing if it's easier.

No, I'll stop. I'll just talk. So Thursday I walked over and looked down into the catch basin, the grate there, and it's packed full of sand. That's the sand and grit they put down on the roads when it's icy. It washed down in there and it just filled up the whole basin, so the water has nowhere to go.
Yeah, that happens, the winter sand settles right in the basin and clogs it up. How deep does the water get out there?

Up to the hubcaps, about. I watched a car go through Friday and it was spraying up on both sides. And the cars that park there, the water's up around the tires the whole time. Then it sits. It holds there about a week before it finally goes down, and then I swear it's barely gone and it starts to build again.
A week. Okay, so this isn't the first time it's built up like this.

No, it's the same thing again. Every time it freezes at night and thaws in the day it gets worse, because the little bit of melt goes to the same spot and it can't drain. And now it's freezing over in the mornings, so Saturday I almost went down on the ice walking to the bus. I'm frustrated, honestly. Somebody should have cleaned that out by now.

I understand. It's a fair thing to be upset about, and it's definitely something we'd send a crew for. They have a truck that vacuums the basins out. Can I get the address, or the nearest cross street to that drain?
Oh, um. I'd rather not give the street over the phone, can you just go off my name and number? It's 401-555-0198.
Hmm, I really do need the location for the crew, otherwise they can't find the right basin. Is there a landmark near it, maybe? A corner, a church, a store?
Let me think. It's near the corner by the little market, the one with the green awning, on my block. Is that enough?

That helps some. I'll write it up with the market and the green awning, and I'll put your number on it so the crew can call if they can't find the basin. And I'll note it's dry-weather, not a storm issue, full of sand.
Yes, thank you. Now, will you open a work order for it? And can you tell me a date? Because I don't want to call back next Monday and have it be, oh, there's nothing on file.

Yes, I'm opening the work order right now while we're talking. As for the date, I don't have a day I can give you. Basin cleanouts get scheduled by the crew supervisor, and he goes by what's been reported. I'd say you're looking at this week or into next, but that's the window. I'll flag it that the water's been standing a week and it's icing up.
This week or next. All right. And will somebody tell me when it's scheduled?

I'll ask them to call you at that number. If you don't hear anything by Friday, call back and give them your name and this work order, and I'll look it up. Let me read the number to you once it comes up. Okay, I have it. Do you have something to write with?
I do. I'm writing it by hand, not typing, don't worry.
Good. It's work order 2-6-0-2-0-2, dash, one.
Two six zero two zero two, dash one. Got it. And you wrote down the sand and the hubcaps?
I did. Catch basin full of sand, water standing about hubcap deep, lasts about a week, no rain involved. And that it's getting icy.
That's right. Okay. Thank you, Denise. You were quick about it.
Of course. Sorry you've been dealing with it. Stay off that ice in the meantime, and call back Friday if you don't hear from the crew.
I will. Thanks. Goodbye.
Bye now.
